title: GET /api/me (just-in-time provisioning) and DELETE /api/me
notes: Scenario: R's shared demo set. Tab IDs come from apps/api/app/engine/fixtures/demo_tabs.json (the 28 tabs in snapshot.example.json); project, claim, note and saved-context IDs come from grove.example.json and memory-search.example.json. IDs these examples create are listed in `introduces`; IDs that belong to another user are listed in `unknown_ids`.
Every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token> unless the example lists request.headers explicitly. user_id never appears in a request body; the server takes it from the token.
Durations are integer milliseconds (active_ms) so every sum is exact; the UI converts to minutes. Times are UTC and follow R's story clock (snapshot at 2026-10-04T11:40:00Z).
Errors are RFC 7807 problem JSON with `instance` = the request path, as in R's files.

user.id is derived from the token, never looked up: uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, 'tabforest:' + tid + ':' + oid); with the fallback login it is the JWT's sub. The fixture above is the user every P example belongs to.

The first GET /api/me creates the users row and a privacy_settings row with defaults (no exclusions, not paused, 90-day retention, cloud AI on) and returns first_sign_in=true, for the first-run onboarding. Later calls return false.
display_name and email come from the token's name and preferred_username claims (the extension requests the profile scope).

stats: total_forests = projects the user has (including past ones); active_goals = projects active in the last 3 days; total_attention_ms = attention summed over projects (a shared tab counts for each project); total_resolved_questions = questions with status resolved. Values agree with grove.example.json and memory-search.example.json.
privacy has the same shape as GET /api/privacy.
A missing, invalid or expired token returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. X-Dev-User is accepted only when AUTH_MODE=dev; on the deployed API a request carrying only X-Dev-User gets 401.

DELETE /api/me removes every row the user owns in every SPEC §8.1 table in one transaction, refreshes the aggregates over the affected range, and returns counts per table and a total. The extension then sends WIPE_LOCAL; the next GET /api/me provisions a fresh account.
